root_cause: Traceback.extract walks the exception chain in a `while True` loop that follows `__cause__` then `__context__` with no cycle check, and recursively calls Traceback.extract for every member of an ExceptionGroup. `raise e from e` makes `e.__cause__ is e`, so the loop re-selects the same exception forever (a hang with growing memory, not a RecursionError; issue #3708). With asyncio TaskGroups a group member's `__context__` points back to the enclosing ExceptionGroup, so the recursive member extract follows context to the group, re-extracts its members, and recurses until RecursionError (issue #3682).
best_solution: In rich/traceback.py Traceback.extract: (1) add a private kwarg `_visited_exceptions: Optional[Set[BaseException]] = None` and bind `grouped_exceptions = set() if None else _visited_exceptions`; (2) in the ExceptionGroup loop skip any member already in the set, add it, and pass `_visited_exceptions=grouped_exceptions` into the recursive extract; (3) follow `__cause__`/`__context__` only when `not grouped_exceptions` (i.e. not inside group extraction), and require `cause is not None and cause is not exc_value` for the cause step. Reasoning from the statement alone: 'traceback recursion' in a traceback renderer means the code that walks exception links (`__cause__`, `__context__`, `.exceptions`) can revisit an exception; those links are arbitrary user-controlled object graphs and can form cycles, so the walker needs a visited set. A self-cycle is created trivially by `raise e from e`.
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_traceback.py::test_recursive_exception: inside `except Exception as e: raise e from e`, then a caller catches it, asserts `e is e.__cause__`, and calls `Console().print_exception(show_locals=True)`. It only needs to terminate without error (no output assertions). Existing traceback tests (chained causes, context, notes, exception groups) must keep passing.
locating_signals: Statement is only the PR title 'Fix traceback recursion' plus two issue URLs; no function, symptom or repro is visible without the linked issue text (issue #3708 contains the MRE and even the proposed `cause is not exc_value` diff). 'traceback' leads to rich/traceback.py; inside it the only loops/recursion over exceptions are the `while True` cause/context walk and the recursive `Traceback.extract` call for ExceptionGroup members in extract().
our_outcome_summary: All four configs FAIL in the Kaggle env (patch_labels resolved=False for all). Test logs for v4/v7/v8 stop after 22 progress characters with no pytest summary, consistent with the new test hanging in the infinite cause loop until the harness timeout. v4: misread 'recursion' as Python RecursionError from deep user recursion; wrapped the install() excepthook in try/except RecursionError and added a repro script; wrong location (the test calls console.print_exception, not the excepthook) and wrong mechanism (self-cause is an infinite while loop, no RecursionError is ever raised). v6: empty patch. v7: only added reproduce_recursion.py (a deep-recursion repro), no source change. v8: wrapped pretty.traverse of frame locals in try/except RecursionError; again the wrong loop, the cause/context walk is untouched so the test still hangs.
generalizable_lesson: When a statement says 'recursion'/'infinite loop'/'hang' about code that walks an object graph (exception __cause__/__context__ chains, parent/child links, references, includes, dependencies), first suspect a missing cycle guard, not stack depth: find every loop or recursive call that follows a link attribute and add a visited set (id() or identity) plus a self-reference check, threading the set through recursive calls. Do not 'fix' it by catching RecursionError at a top-level entry point. Build a repro with the smallest cycle (x.link = x, e.g. `raise e from e`) and run it under a timeout, since the failure is a hang rather than a traceback.
acceptable_alternatives: For the hidden test alone, changing the cause step to `if cause is not None and cause is not exc_value:` (the diff proposed in issue #3708) is sufficient because Python leaves `__context__` unset for a self-raise and `raise ... from` sets `__suppress_context__`. More robust: keep a `seen` set of id(exc) across the whole while loop and stop when the next cause/context is already seen (also handles A->B->A cycles, which gold does not), and pass the set into the recursive ExceptionGroup extract so group-member context cycles terminate.
